newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombian rebels force closure of cement plant.
newsitem.headline: Colombian rebels force closure of cement plant.

text.p: Leftist rebels forced the shutdown of a cement factory in northwest Colombia after dynamiting electric pylons in a bid to pressure its directors to pay a "war tax," authorities said on Wednesday.
Cementos Rioclaro said they had laid off all 350 workers at their plant in Puerto Triunfo in Antioquia province because of the attacks by National Liberation Army (ELN) rebels.

Gov. Alvaro Uribe praised the factory management for refusing to accede to rebel demands and army chiefs said they were stepping up counterinsurgency operations in the zone. "We're aware that the guerrillas are trying to extort Cementos Rioclaro but fortunately the management decided not to pay. We're mobilising troops and our aim is to continue defeating the guerrillas in all areas of the province," Uribe said.

Colombia's leftist guerrilla groups have a long practice of demanding financial contributions from medium and large businesses in conflict zones in return for not disrupting their operations. Failure to pay may meet with sabotage and kidnapping of employees.
In some zones, this so-called war tax is said to extend to demanding money from drug traffickers to protect clandestine narcotics laboratories and illict plantations.
At least 13 electricity pylons leading to the cement factory have been blown up by rebels in recent days, causing an estimated $230 million in damage, according to a local government spokesman.

This is the second time this year that the company, part of the Sindicato Antioqueno industrial conglomerate, has found itself subject to guerrilla violence. Three foreign engineers checking machinery at the Puerto Triunfo plant were kidnapped in February. One, a German, was released quickly but the other two were freed only last month after their parent company in Denmark was thought to have paid a hefty ransom.

In a recent interview, company chairman Luis Fernando Ochoa said Cementos Rioclaro never paid the ELN war tax but spent about $200,000 a year on social programmes in the area. He was unavailable for comment on the latest attacks.
